'''Joseph Michael Young''' (born June 27, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Qingdao Eagles]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). The son of former [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) player [[Michael Young (basketball, born 1961)|Michael Young]],<ref name="Houston bio">{{cite web |title=Joseph Young Bio |work=uhcougars.com |url=http://www.uhcougars.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/young_joseph00.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150403005850/http://www.uhcougars.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/young_joseph00.html |archive-date=2015-04-03 |url-status=dead |access-date=2015-03-09 }}</ref> he played [[college basketball]] with the [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston Cougars]] and later the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks]]. Young earned third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors and was named [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|conference player of the year]] in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]] as a senior with Oregon in 2015. He was selected by the [[Indiana Pacers]] in the second round of the [[2015 NBA draft]] with the 43rd overall pick.

==High school career==
Young attended [[Yates High School]] under Greg Wise, where he averaged 27.5 points, 4.1 rebounds, 4.4 steals and 3.8 assists per game as a senior to help lead the Lions to a perfect 34–0 record and the No. 1 national ranking in final polls from USA Today, MaxPreps and Rivals.com. In the process, he was named to the Parade All-America Third-Team, the Texas Gatorade Boys’ Basketball Player of the Year and the Class 4A Texas Association of Basketball Coaches All-State Team. Yates ended up winning their second straight State Championship with Young winning the Most Valuable Player of the state final award.<ref name="Houston bio" /><ref name="Oregon bio">{{cite web|url=http://www.goducks.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209278100|title=Oregon bio|work=GoDucks.com|access-date=December 12, 2015}}</ref>

==College career==
Young originally committed to [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]], but was forced to sit out a season after fired head coach [[Keno Davis]] refused to release him from his letter of intent. He began his collegiate career at [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]], where his father was Director of Basketball Operations. As a sophomore, Young averaged 18 points per game and shot 42 percent from the three-point arc and 87 percent on free throws. After the season, his father refused reassignment at the University of Houston and left the program, and Young opted to transfer.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Phillips|first1=Scott|title=Houston leading scorer Joseph Young, and father Michael, leaving the program|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/06/01/houston-leading-scorer-joseph-young-and-father-michael-leaving-the-program/|access-date=June 7, 2015|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=June 1, 2013}}</ref> Young announced his intention to transfer to Oregon to play under coach [[Dana Altman]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Goodman|first1=Jeff|title=Oregon lands guard Joseph Young|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/9433570/houston-cougars-transfer-joseph-young-lands-oregon-ducks|access-date=June 7, 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|date=June 28, 2013}}</ref> In 2015, he was named the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Conference Player of the Year]] after averaging 19.8 points, 4.5 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game as a senior. He hit back-to-back game-winning shots versus [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]] and [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Alger|first=Tyson|title=Dana Altman and Joseph Young named Pac-12's coach and player of the year|date=March 9, 2015|newspaper=The Oregonian|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/index.ssf/2015/03/dana_altman_and_joseph_young_n.html|access-date=March 9, 2015}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Indiana Pacers (2015–2018)===
On June 25, 2015, Young was selected with the 43rd pick of the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/pacers-add-turner-young-2015-draft|title=Pacers Add Turner, Young in 2015 Draft|date=June 26, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 25, 2015}}</ref> After leading the [[2015 NBA Summer League]] in scoring with 22.5 points per game and earning All-Tournament honors, Young signed a four-year, $4 million deal with the Pacers on July 14.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/joe-young-signs-contract|title=Joe Young Signs Contract|date=July 14, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 14, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Meagher|first1=Sean|title=Joseph Young, Indiana Pacers reportedly agree on 4-year rookie deal|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/nba/index.ssf/2015/07/joseph_young_pacers_reportedly.html#incart_story_package|access-date=July 14, 2015|work=The Oregonian|date=July 13, 2015}}</ref> On December 11, 2015, he was assigned to the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/pacers-assign-joe-young-mad-ants|title=Pacers Assign Joe Young 2017|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 11, 2017}}</ref>

=== Nanjing Monkey King (2018–2020) ===
On August 1, 2018, Young signed a one-year deal with [[Nanjing Monkey King]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).<ref>{{cite web |last1=East |first1=Tony |title=Joe Young will leave the NBA and go play in China |url=https://8points9seconds.com/2018/08/01/joe-young-indiana-pacers-china/ |publisher=8 Points 9 Seconds |access-date=August 1, 2018 |date=August 1, 2018}}</ref> In his first career game with the CBA, Young recorded 23 points, 5 rebounds and 5 assists in a 91–118 loss to the Qingdao Eagles.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2018/1021_7300_14428.asp|title=Qingdao Eagles 118 – Nanjing Monkey King 91|publisher=Eurobasket|date=October 21, 2018|access-date=January 13, 2020}}</ref> On November 15, 2018, Young recorded a career-high 51 points to go along with 9 rebounds and 2 assists in a 110–124 loss to the [[Jilin Northeast Tigers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2018/1115_14428_2929.asp|title=Nanjing Monkey King 110 – Jilin Tigers 124|publisher=Eurobasket|date=November 15, 2018|access-date=January 13, 2020}}</ref>

On June 27, 2019, Young was included in the [[2019 NBA Summer League]] roster of the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Lakers Announce 2019 Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/lakers-announce-2019-summer-leagues-roster|date=June 27, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=June 27, 2019}}</ref> He re-signed with Nanjing for the [[2019–20 Chinese Basketball Association season|2019–20 season]],<ref>{{cite news|last1=Carchia|first1=Emiliano|title=Joe Young to re-sign with Nanjing Money King|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/joe-young-to-re-sign-with-nanjing-money-king|date=August 1, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|access-date=August 1, 2019}}</ref>

On July 23, 2020, Young dropped 74 points against Shandong Heroes during one of the final regular season games in the CBA's bubble en route to being named the league's regular season scoring champion. Young marked the third-highest personal single-game scoring show in CBA history.<ref>{{Cite web|last=刘小卓|title=Young scores 74 in Nanjing's loss, Beijing win 6th straight|url=https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202007/14/WS5f0d1453a310834817259424.html|access-date=2020-12-07|website=www.chinadaily.com.cn}}</ref>

=== Beijing Royal Fighters (2020–2021) ===
On October 1, 2020, Young signed with the [[Beijing Royal Fighters]] of the CBA for an annual salary of $3.1 million. Young will be playing under former NBA All-Star and CBA legend, Stephon Marbury.

Young is coming off a career season where he averaged a league high of 38.3 points, 6.4 assists and 2.3 steals per game for Nanjing Tongxi Monkey Kings.<ref>{{cite web |title=Royal Fighters ink Joseph Young |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/646213/Royal-Fighters-ink-Joseph-Young |website=Asiabasket |access-date=October 1, 2020 |date=October 1, 2020}}</ref>

===Birmingham Squadron (2021–2022)===
On October 25, 2021, Young joined the [[Birmingham Squadron]] through a trade.<ref>{{cite web|title=Birmingham Squadron finalize roster for team's first training camp in Birmingham|url=https://birmingham.gleague.nba.com/news/birmingham-squadron-announce-2021-training-camp-roster/|work=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2021|access-date=November 2, 2021}}</ref>

===Promitheas Patras (2022–2023)===
On July 22, 2022, Young, according to his agent [[Pete Mickeal]], signed with [[Promitheas Patras B.C.|Promitheas Patras]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]], his first European club. On January 4, 2023, he parted ways with the Greek club. He averaged 16 points, 2.2 rebounds and 2.2 assists in domestic competition, as well as 23.4 points and 3.9 assists in the EuroCup.

=== Napoli (2023) ===
On January 5, 2023, Young signed with [[Napoli Basket (2016)|Napoli]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/joe-young-signs-with-gevi-napoli/|title=Joe Young signs with GeVi Napoli|last=|first=|date=January 5, 2023|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=January 8, 2023 |last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref>

=== Fujian Sturgeons (2024–2025) ===
On July 4, 2024, Young signed with [[Homenetmen Beirut (basketball)|Homenetmen Beirut]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=هومنتمن يدعم صفوفه بصفقة أمريكية |url=https://www.kooora.com/?n=1339917 |publisher=Kooora.com |access-date=18 September 2024 |date=4 July 2024}}</ref>

On September 30, 2024, Young signed with the [[Fujian Sturgeons]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).<ref>{{cite web |title=Young comes back to Sturgeons, ex Gorgan |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/893510/Young-comes-back-to-Sturgeons,-ex-Gorgan |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=3 October 2024 |date=30 September 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
The son of Tina and [[Michael Young (basketball, born 1961)|Michael Young]], his father ranks as the third-leading scorer in [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston Cougars]] history and is one of five players to have his jersey number retired by the school. He majored in sociology.<ref name="Houston bio" /><ref name="Oregon bio" /> His younger brother [[Jacob Young (basketball)|Jacob]] played college basketball for [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] and [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]] before transferring to [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Kratch|first=James|title=Rutgers lands Texas transfer Jacob Young|date=April 22, 2018|website=NJ.com|url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersbasketball/index.ssf/2018/04/rutgers_lands_texas_transfer_jacob_young_what_it_m.html|access-date=October 4, 2018}}</ref> Young and [[Paul George]] are fifth [[cousin]]s.<ref>{{cite news|last=Hunsinger Benbow|first=Dana|title=Pacers' 2nd round pick Joe Young related to Paul George?|date=June 30, 2015|newspaper=Indianapolis Star|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2015/06/30/pacers-joe-young-is-paul-georges-cousin/29509753/|access-date=October 4, 2018}}</ref>

=== Philanthropy ===
Young has remained involved in the Houston, Texas community and in 2019 donated 1,000 Thanksgiving Day turkey dinners to less fortunate residents of the city's Midtown district.
